chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Sa'id al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about kissing the Stone from the side of the door. He said, 'Is it not that you only intend to kiss the corner?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'It suffices you wherever your hand reaches.' And it suffices him if he is unable to kiss it to point to it with his finger. He narrated that.

key_terms.الرُّكْنَ: The Corner (specifically the South Corner of the Kaaba)
key_terms.يُجْزِيكَ: It suffices you / It is accepted

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one cannot reach the Black Stone to kiss it during Tawaf?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the essence of the ritual is honoring the Rukn (corner), allowing for flexibility in Tawaf where physical proximity to the Black Stone is difficult. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of ease (taysir), permitting pointing with a finger if direct contact is impossible, thereby prioritizing the spiritual intent over rigid physical constraints. This flexibility is particularly relevant in crowded conditions or for those with limited mobility, ensuring the act remains accessible to all worshippers.
